Q: how to control verbosity of modules auto-load action? A:

It is indeed surprising that -Verbose:$false isn't also honored by the implicitly loaded modules that are the dependencies of a given module loaded with Import-Module.

You can work around the problem by replacing Import-Module Helper -Verbose:$false with:

& {
  $VerbosePreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
  Import-Module Helper # Now Helper as well as its dependencies import quietly.
}

Note:

  • Calling a script block ({ ... }) with & executes the enclosed code in a child scope, which is a convenient way to limit the effect of $VerbosePreference = 'SilentlyContinue' to that code.

  • If you wanted to use -Scope Local with Import-Module to limit the import to the calling script, you'd have to set $VerbosePreference directly in the script scope and save and restore its original value.

Q: sorting arrays of arrays of ints (2-d array) does not work (it sorts as strings; 1-d arrays work) A:

You might use a BigInt (biginteger) type for this (available from PowerShell 7).

  • Every Int in the array is 32 bits
    (I am not considering any negative values therefore you might even take 31 bits)
  • Meaning, to define a comparable value, you need to do the following:
    • for each Int in the array, shift any prior Ints 32 bits to the left
      (-shl 32 or: *= [Math]::pow(2,32)) and add it to the current value.
$a1 = [int[]](10,1)
$a2 = [int[]](2,1)
$a3 = [int[]](1,11,0)
$a4 = [int[]](3)

$a1, $a2, $a3, $a4 | Sort-Object {
    $BigInt = [BigInt]0
    foreach ($Int in $_) {
        $BigInt = $BigInt -shl 32
        $BigInt += $Int
    }
    $BigInt
} | ForEach-Object { "$_" }

3
2 1
10 1
1 11 0

In case you want int arrays of different sizes ordered as if they where strings, you probably want to simply pad each value to the max string length of an int: (([int]::MaxValue).ToString().Length):

$Digits = ([int]::MaxValue).ToString().Length

$a1 = [int[]](10,1)
$a2 = [int[]](2,1)
$a3 = [int[]](1,11,0)
$a4 = [int[]](3)

$a1, $a2, $a3, $a4 | Sort-Object {
    foreach ($Int in $_) { $Int.ToString("D$Digits") }
} | ForEach-Object { "$_" }

1 11 0
2 1
3
10 1

Q: How to filter out rows that is less than 5 decimal places on 4 float 64 columns? A: 
-- I don't know if I'm missing something here but at least in Oracle 19 it's quite simple.
-- Example:
WITH DATASET AS (
SELECT CAST(0.123456 AS FLOAT) A FROM DUAL
UNION ALL
SELECT CAST(0.12345 AS FLOAT) A FROM DUAL
UNION ALL
SELECT CAST(0.1234 AS FLOAT) A FROM DUAL

)
SELECT A FROM DATASET
WHERE A = ROUND(A, 5);
Output:
A
-------
0.12345
0.1234
